model_output.verdict: A healthcare COO whose resume connects a substantial operating remit with measurable improvements.
write_up: This is a strong COO resume! At Lakeshore Dental Partners, you show how the organization grew from 38 to 140 practices alongside an improvement in same-store margin. Across your healthcare roles, you pair the work you led with figures a recruiter can use to understand it.

The new-practice integration line is a great model: it names the change you made and shows the time before and after. Your progression from clinic operations to COO is easy to follow, and your current team, revenue, P&L and board responsibilities are right up front.

I'd tighten two earlier lines by adding what drove the shorter appointment wait and what the Epic go-live changed, if you can. Your resume is unlikely to be the thing holding you back; the fit with a particular healthcare organization and competition for the role will matter too.

cards.line: - Cut new-practice integration time from 7 months to 10 weeks by standardizing the 90-day integration playbook
cards.cannot_tell: Keep this as a model. A recruiter can see the operating change you made and compare the time it took before and after.

cards.where: Senior Vice President, Operations, wait time line
cards.line: - Reduced patient wait time to third available appointment from 21 days to 6 across primary care
cards.cannot_tell: The improvement is substantial, but a recruiter can't tell what you changed to reduce the wait. That detail would show how you approached access across primary care.
cards.example: Reduced patient wait time to third available appointment from 21 days to 6 across primary care by [what you changed]
cards.question: What did you change to reduce the wait for an appointment?

cards.where: Vice President, Clinic Operations, Epic line
cards.line: - Led the Epic go-live across the clinics in 2013
cards.cannot_tell: Leading the go-live names the project, but not what changed for the clinics. Add the result you can point to.
cards.example: Led the Epic go-live across the clinics in 2013, resulting in [what changed]
cards.question: What changed for the clinics after the Epic go-live?

fit.why: Your headline and current role name you as a Chief Operating Officer, with responsibility for practices, employees and the P&L.
fit.level: Executive, leads operations for 140 practices and owns the $410M P&L with the CFO
fit.note: Your experience points toward executive operations roles in multi-site healthcare, especially organizations growing through acquisitions and new openings. Your board reporting and operating model work are also prominent.
